title: Kusum Mishra v. State of U.P.
coram: Tarun Agarwala and Siddhartha Varma, JJ.
disposition: Writ disposed; bill-correction representation treated as cl. 6.5; EE to decide in four weeks.
headnote: A consumer's representation seeking correction of an electricity bill may be treated as an application under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, with the Executive Engineer directed to pass an appropriate order within a fixed time, the High Court not deciding the bill on merits.
facts: Kusum Mishra filed a writ petition in the Allahabad High Court against an electricity bill, relying on a representation already made for its correction. The Division Bench did not examine the bill on merits. It treated the representation as an application under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, directed the Executive Engineer to pass an appropriate order within four weeks of presentation of a certified copy of the order, and disposed of the writ petition.

holding_units.holding: A representation seeking correction of an electricity bill is to be treated as an application under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the Executive Engineer is to pass an appropriate order thereon within the time fixed by the Court.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the impugned electricity bill
not_decided.note: Merits of the bill-correction claim were left to the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5.
